title: Lesson 64: Fine-tuning vs RAG: The Decision Framework
description: The framework for choosing between retrieval augmented generation, which hands the model new knowledge at answer time without touching its weights, and fine-tuning, which bakes durable behavior into the weights. It covers the mechanism that separates them, the five-question decision framework, the watchouts on each side, and the hybrid pattern that fine-tunes behavior while retrieving current facts.

questions.question: A company's agent answers plausibly but wrongly because the pricing catalog it needs changed last month, and it also writes replies in a flat voice it cannot seem to fix with better prompting. Applying the lesson's core distinction, which statement is correct?
options: Both gaps are behavior gaps, so fine-tuning alone is the right answer and retrieval adds nothing.
The stale-facts gap is a knowledge problem best handled by RAG because it can cite and stay current, while the flat-voice gap is a behavior problem that fine-tuning is suited to carry in weights.
Both gaps are knowledge gaps, so a single RAG pipeline fixes everything without any model training.
Neither approach can address both, so the system should avoid using its own data entirely.
questions.explanation: The lesson's core distinction is that RAG changes what the model sees and fine-tuning changes how it behaves. Missing or stale catalog facts are a knowledge gap that retrieval handles, because indexed today's or yesterday's data appears at inference time with no retraining. A flat, off-brand voice is a behavior gap that a fine-tuned model can carry reliably in its weights. The lesson emphasizes this is the one-line rule: fine-tuning adjusts behavior, style, and format, while retrieval is the tool for current facts.

questions.question: For a legal assistant whose statutes change several times a quarter, needs to cite the exact source document behind every answer, and must withhold certain cases from users without clearance, which choice does the lesson's framework favor first and why?
options: Fine-tuning, because baking the statutes into model weights makes answers faster with no retrieval infrastructure to maintain.
Fine-tuning, because a trained model can reliably reproduce legal terminology, which is more important than currency.
RAG, because the knowledge changes frequently, answers must be traceable to a source, and per-user access control is enforced by the retrieval layer.
RAG only if the company has many labeled question-answer pairs; the framework ranks that above freshness and citations.
questions.explanation: The framework's questions two and three push toward RAG. Knowledge that changes frequently favors retrieval because indexed updates appear with no retraining. RAG also supplies provenance, since the retrieved passage is passed explicitly and can be cited, and it honors per-user access because the retrieval layer can withhold segments a user is not permitted to see, something baked-in weights cannot do. Labeled pairs affect whether fine-tuning is feasible, but they do not outweigh the freshness, citation, and access-control requirements the scenario sets.

questions.question: A team fine-tunes a model on its invoice-processing workflow so the output format is always valid JSON, and separately builds a RAG layer that supplies the currently approved pricing and tax tables at inference time. Which statement best matches the lesson's guidance on this design?
options: This is the hybrid pattern the lesson recommends: fine-tune the durable behavior, retrieve the current facts, and the two together beat either approach alone for complex use cases.
This is wasteful because fine-tuning already carries the pricing data in its weights, so the RAG layer is redundant.
Fine-tuning and RAG should never be combined, since retrieval context overrides anything the model learned.
The RAG layer should be removed because an output-format model produces identical results whether or not it receives context.
questions.explanation: The repeated example in the lesson, the support agent, uses exactly this split, and the sourcing states it as the mature enterprise default: a fine-tuned model handles domain understanding and output format while RAG supplies the latest facts at inference time, and the combination outperforms either alone for complex use cases. The JSON formatting is a durable behavior for fine-tuning to own, while the pricing and tax tables are current facts that belong in the retrieval layer.
